title: A CHANGED FILE BREAKS THE SAVED PROMISE
question: Why save a bundle and later verify it with --run-root?
takeaway: The saved bundle remembers each referenced file's byte identity, so a later edit becomes a named mismatch instead of a silent change.

reading_speeds.at_2_seconds: A green saved fingerprint and a red later fingerprint do not match.
reading_speeds.at_20_seconds: Bundle records result.json as it exists at baseline time; verify --run-root re-hashes the later file and names the mismatch.
reading_speeds.at_2_minutes: The story demonstrates post-baseline mutation detection while preserving the limits of an unsigned, retrospectively created baseline.

medium.rationale: The baseline/later timeline, exact mismatch message, and proof boundary require deterministic, source-verifiable text.

labels.claim: Bundle validates and writes canonical evidence JSON with referenced-file hashes.
A referenced source file whose bytes are hashed into its input record.
The baseline input record stores the file's SHA-256 value.
A later mutation can change the retained source bytes after the baseline was stored.
Verify with run root re-hashes referenced local files.
The comparison uses the digest saved in the bundle.
The comparison recomputes the local file digest at verification time.
A referenced-file digest difference is reported as an error and verify returns one.

labels.text: Referenced file digest mismatch for result.json
labels.claim: This is the exact error form produced for a changed referenced file.
A separately retained baseline is required to detect later source mutation.

boundaries: A retrospective first bundle proves only what the archive contained when bundled.
Anyone who edits an unsigned bundle can recompute its internal digest.
A byte mismatch detects change; it does not identify who changed the file or which version is true.

accessibility.alt_text: At baseline time, result.json is hashed into a separately stored evidence bundle. After the file changes, verify with run root computes a different hash and reports a referenced-file digest mismatch with exit 1.
accessibility.long_description: A three-act horizontal timeline begins with Save the Baseline: result.json with reward one is connected to a saved SHA-256 fingerprint inside evidence.json. In act two the file changes to reward zero and receives a different current fingerprint. In act three verify --run-root compares expected and actual fingerprints, shows a not-equal sign, and reports the exact result.json digest mismatch. A footer says to store the bundle separately and explains that detection is not attribution or truth.
